common.unreachable: The server can’t be reached. Check the connection and try again.
common.unreadable: The server’s answer couldn’t be read. Try again, or tell an admin.
common.notAllowed: You don’t have permission to see or do this. An admin can grant it.
common.notFound: Not found. It may have been archived, or the link is wrong.
common.limited: Too many tries. Wait {seconds} seconds, then try again.
common.name: Name

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.codeHint: Six digits. A code works once.
signIn.refused: That email address and password don’t match a login that may sign in here, or the login is waiting after wrong tries. Check them and try again.
signIn.codeNeeded: Your password is right. Now type the code your authenticator app shows.
signIn.ended: Your session ended. Sign in again to carry on.

reset.title: Reset your password
reset.about: Type the email address the firm holds for you. If it signs in here, a code is sent to it.
reset.sent: If that address signs in here, a code is on its way. It works once, for a short while.
reset.noMail: This installation sends no email. Ask an admin to set a new password for you.
reset.done: Your password is set. Sign in with it.
reset.refusedCode: That code isn’t good: it may have been used, run out, or been mistyped. Ask for another.
reset.mismatch: The two passwords aren’t the same.

password.title: Change your password
password.required: Somebody else set your password. Choose one of your own before anything else.
password.hint: At least the length the firm asks for. A long phrase is best; no other rules.
password.done: Your password is changed. Your other sessions are ended.
password.unchanged: The new password is the same as the one you have.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords aren’t the same.

twoStep.title: Set up two-step sign-in
twoStep.required: Admins and managers need an authenticator app to sign in. Set one up now.
twoStep.optional: An authenticator app keeps your login safe even if your password is known.
twoStep.keyToType: In your authenticator app, add a login and type this key:
twoStep.uri: Or, where your app takes a link:
twoStep.refused: That code doesn’t prove the app has the key, or the setup ran out. Begin again.
twoStep.removed: Two-step sign-in is removed from your login.
twoStep.removeCode: Code your app shows now, to remove it

account.title: Your account
account.sessionsAbout: Each place you’re signed in. End one you don’t recognise; this one ends when you sign out.

home.title: Projects
home.about: Pick a project to work on it.
home.name: Project

queued.one: 1 ticket is queued to be drawn again with the change.
queued.other: {count} tickets are queued to be drawn again with the change.

lockedLeft.one: 1 ticket locked as invoiced keeps what it had.
lockedLeft.other: {count} tickets locked as invoiced keep what they had.

clients.title: Clients
clients.about: The jurisdictions and agencies that pay for cleanup. A client is kept across disasters and archived, never deleted.
clients.name: Client

events.title: Declaration events
events.about: The disasters and their references. Many clients’ projects can point at one declaration event.
events.name: Declaration event
events.referenceHint: As it is written: DR-9001-FL, a state or local declaration, or your own code.

contractors.title: Contractors
contractors.about: Hauling companies and the firm’s own subs. A prime holds a contract on a project; a sub is typed in at certification.
contractors.name: Contractor

lists.title: The firm’s lists
lists.about: Every pick-list the firm extends. Monitors pick these values by name. A built-in value can be renamed but not archived; nothing is deleted.
lists.requiresRoeHint: Every collection, unit rate ticket and survey on a project of this program type carries an ROE.
lists.photosByStageHint: Its tickets take a pre-work, a measurement and a post-work photograph.

useNames.BACK_OFFICE_RECORD: A record made in the back office

lists.fieldTagsOnProject: Field tags belong to one project: pick the project in the header to add them on its setup page.

newProject.title: A new project
newProject.name: Project name
newProject.nameHint: As the contract names it: Bayline County ROW, Hurricane Delphine.
newProject.timeZoneHint: Every ticket’s time is read in it.
newProject.activeToHint: Leave empty while the end isn’t known.
newProject.numbersFromHint: Where none is given, tickets start at 100,001 and ROEs at 1. Cert numbers start where the firm says, a number that doesn’t look made up.

projectSetup.title: Project setup
projectSetup.about: This project’s settings, its active window, how it numbers its tickets, its field tags, and its primes and contracts.
projectSetup.loadCallLow: Flag a load call at or under (%)
projectSetup.loadCallHigh: Flag a load call at or over (%)
projectSetup.loadCallHint: Leave empty to turn this check off. A load call of 0% is always flagged.
projectSetup.stumpRootBallWider: Check that a stump’s root ball is wider than the stump
projectSetup.stumpFillNeedsExposure: Check that a stump paid by fill is half or more exposed
projectSetup.siteCircle: A site’s circle where it has no shape (feet)
projectSetup.siteCircleHint: How far from the site’s GPS a load still counts as at the site.
projectSetup.fieldTagsAbout: Back-office labels, set by correction and read by the Field tag criterion and the exports. Phones never take one.
projectSetup.signedCopyHint: An https:// address where the signed contract is kept.

forms.title: Forms
forms.about: One form per kind of document. Debris types are added to a load or haul-out form as the contract names the work; surveys, ROEs, incidents and drop-off logs may carry the firm’s own fields.
forms.name: Form
forms.hiddenHint: Kept for the back office and the rules; monitors don’t see it.
forms.noFields: No fields of the firm’s own yet.
forms.newDebrisType: A new debris type for the firm’s library
forms.newDebrisTypeHint: Added to the library, then picked here.

payItems.title: Pay items
payItems.about: Each priced line of the contract as set up: its code, the firm’s description, the work it prices, its unit and a rate for each prime. The only place a rate lives.
payItems.kindOfWorkHint: Only for a unit rate pay item.
payItems.monitorMayMarkIneligible: The monitor may mark it ineligible
payItems.quantityFromCarriedTickets: Quantity from the tickets a load carries
payItems.rateHint: Up to four decimals. Leave empty where this prime has none.

rules.title: Rules
rules.about: The firm’s pricing: each rule names one contract and runs only on its prime’s tickets. When every “if” holds, its actions add or remove numbered transactions, or void the ticket. All passing rules run, in number order.
rules.name: Rule

sites.title: Disposal sites
sites.about: Where debris legally goes on this project: each with its type, what it does (its site facts), its permit, GPS and area.
sites.name: Site
sites.ineligibleHint: Tickets there are flagged and still bill.
sites.coordinateHint: Decimal degrees, up to eight places.
sites.label: Label
sites.linkFee: Link a tipping fee pay item
sites.lookupAbout: Worked out from the setup as it stands: for each debris type and prime, the load call, the scale weight, a count of the tickets carried, or nothing more.

asks.CARRIED_COUNT: A count of the tickets carried

map.title: Project map
map.about: The project’s boundary and its zones. Reconciliation attaches a zone from each ticket’s GPS; outside the boundary is flagged.
map.esriHint: An https:// address of a feature layer.
map.accessTokenLabel: Access token, where the layer asks for one
map.picture: The project’s boundary with {count} zones and its sites

certifications.title: Certifications
certifications.about: Each certified container or crew. The cert number is the placard and the badge. Capacity is worked out by the server from the measured boxes; nobody types it.
certifications.subHint: As written on the form; leave empty where there is none.
certifications.reason: Why it’s entered in the back office

roes.title: ROEs
roes.about: Rights of Entry, from the phones or from paper. The scope is entered here from the paper: the debris types and the unit rate work the owner allowed.

setupCheck.title: Setup check
setupCheck.about: Gaps in the setup before the field day: each said plainly. Nothing here stops field work.
setupCheck.none: No gaps: the setup is complete as far as the check can see.

photos.missing: This photograph’s file hasn’t arrived yet.

people.title: People
people.about: The firm’s back office, its field monitors and the read-only viewers it issues. Nobody is deleted: a person who left is archived, and everything they made still names them.
people.name: Name
people.monitorsAbout: Field monitors are created on a phone, online, under the master passcode.
people.permissionsAbout: What this manager or analyst may see and do. A permission taken away refuses their very next request. An act needs its area’s view beside it.
people.setPasswordAbout: They choose their own at their next sign-in. Their sessions end now.
people.clearTwoStepAbout: For one who lost the phone that held their authenticator: they set it up again at their next sign-in.
people.noHistory: No assignments in the last 30 days.

firmSettings.title: The firm’s settings
firmSettings.about: Settings for the whole installation. Each change is audited with its note.
firmSettings.phoneKey: Revoke a lost phone’s key after (hours)
firmSettings.phoneKeyHint: Leave empty to keep a lost phone’s key until it is turned in.
firmSettings.viewerTwoStep: Read-only viewers must use two-step sign-in
firmSettings.passcodeAbout: One per firm: it enrols phones and is the offline fallback. Changing it takes your own password; each phone takes the new one when it next syncs.
firmSettings.passcodeChanged: The master passcode is changed: version {version}.
firmSettings.reportContactHint: Printed on the daily report’s last page, for a reader who wants to be added to its list. Empty prints none.

phones.title: Phones
phones.about: Every enrolled phone. A phone is enrolled once; its work comes from each day’s assignment. One lost or retired is out of service until it is returned.
phones.name: Phone

kinds.AS_MONITOR: By the master passcode, as the monitor

dispatch.title: Dispatch board
dispatch.about: Each person’s work for the day: their ticket types, their one site where the work is at one, and their phone. A phone takes its monitor’s assignment at sign-in. Nothing here stops work.

origins.UNPLANNED: On the phone, under the master passcode

hours.title: Time clock
hours.about: Workers’ own hours, by their assignment. The day ends before midnight in the project’s time zone: what is worked past it counts on the next day. A manager approves a day; an approved day is locked until it is unlocked with a note.
hours.noDays: No time clock entries in these days.

causes.WORK_TIME_AFTER_RECEIVED: Work time after it was received
causes.WORK_TIME_BEFORE_ENROLMENT: Work time before the phone was enrolled
causes.QUANTITY_MISSING_FOR_PAY_ITEM: Quantity missing for a pay item
causes.FILL_WITHOUT_EXPOSED_ROOT_BALL: Fill without an exposed root ball

queue.title: Review queue
queue.waitingBeside: What else waits for a person

jobsWaiting.one: 1 ticket waits on a job set aside
jobsWaiting.other: {count} tickets wait on a job set aside

queue.newFieldEvent: Make a field event (a phone failed)
queue.caption: {workflow}: tickets waiting for a person
queue.waitingOnJob: Waiting on a job set aside: its lines may be stale until the job is put back.

ticket.title: {workflow} ticket {number}
ticket.lockedNotice: This ticket is locked as invoiced. A person who may unlock it unlocks it first, before anything on it changes.
ticket.closedNotice: This project is closed: nothing on it changes until an admin reopens it.
ticket.voidAbout: A void keeps the record and stops all its billing. Void what never happened; real work under the wrong number is renumbered.
ticket.reprocessAbout: The worker draws the ticket’s conclusions again from its field events and the setup as they stand. Nothing is changed.
ticket.makeHere: Make a field event under this number
ticket.noFlags: No flag stands on this ticket.
ticket.unitRateConcluded: A unit rate ticket is its one field event: its lines are below.
ticket.noCompleted: No completed record yet: the ticket waits for its other field event, or for the worker.

event.title: {kind} {number}
event.certNotFound: {number} (no certification with this number on the project)
event.payItemHint: Left empty, the system works it out from the payable type and the measurement.
event.rootBallHalfExposed: Root ball half or more exposed
event.roeNotFound: {number} (no ROE with this number on the project)
event.fieldTagHint: A back-office label: no phone takes one.
event.correctAbout: Change only what was keyed wrong. The value before is kept in the history, and the ticket is worked again.
event.renumberAbout: Renumber real work recorded under the wrong number. Never renumber work that never happened: void it.
event.photoRemoved: Removed from the record; still kept.

made.title: Make a field event
made.about: Make a field event here only when a phone failed. It pairs by its number like any other, and is flagged as made in the back office with your name and the reason.
made.splitSuffixHint: A split’s property or pile: A, B…; empty on a whole load.

history.notProcessed: The worker couldn’t process this ticket on this run.

waiting.unreadable: What was sent couldn’t be read

quarantine.title: Quarantined records
quarantine.about: A record a phone sent under a number another record already holds. Read it beside the one that holds the number, then give real work the number it should have had, or mark a second copy of the same record. Never renumber work that never happened.

reasons.DUPLICATE_FIELD_EVENT: Another field event of its kind holds the number

quarantine.renumberAbout: It is saved as a record of its own under the number it should have had, written as you, with its photographs; its ticket is worked again.
quarantine.secondCopyAbout: Nothing is made from it. It stays as sent, marked with your name.

held.title: Held records
held.about: What a phone sent that couldn’t be saved, exactly as sent, with why and what its phone was told. Save it as it should be, or close it.
held.closeAbout: Nothing is made from it. It stays as sent, with its photographs and your note.
held.record: The record as it should be
held.recordHint: As the phone sends it (JSON). Change only what is wrong.
held.notJson: That isn’t JSON: check the brackets and quotes. Nothing was saved.
held.notRecord: That isn’t a record a phone sends ({problem}). Nothing was saved.

files.title: Files set aside
files.about: A file a phone sent for a photograph that wasn’t the file it fingerprinted. It is kept beside the photograph, never as its file. Close it when the photograph’s own file won’t come.
files.closeAbout: The photograph’s own file won’t come. This one stays, kept beside it, never as its file.

jobs.title: Jobs set aside
jobs.about: A job of the worker that failed too often is set aside, and its tickets wait for a person. Put it back to have them worked again, nothing changed; a ticket locked as invoiced is left as it is.
jobs.putBackAbout: Its tickets are worked again as their records and the setup stand.

surveys.title: Surveys
surveys.about: Pre-work and post-work surveys, as their phones made them or as entered here from paper. A survey never bills.

incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.about: Incidents, as their phones made them or as entered here from paper. An incident is on no ticket and never bills.

dropOffLogs.title: Citizen drop-off logs
dropOffLogs.about: A drop-off at a site, as its phone logged it or as entered here from paper. It has no quantity and never bills: the pile bills when it is hauled out.
dropOffLogs.add: Enter a drop-off log from paper

tickets.title: QC and invoice lock
tickets.about: Pick tickets to set their QC status, or to lock them as invoiced in a batch. Only a completed, QC Approved ticket locks; each one that can’t says why.
tickets.caption: {workflow}: every ticket
tickets.unlockAbout: The lock is kept, marked unlocked with your name. The ticket is worked again as the setup stands now.
tickets.lockAbout: A batch is optional: a ticket is locked all the same. Each ticket is locked on its own; one that can’t be is said, and the rest are locked.

batches.title: Invoice batches
batches.about: A batch is a name and its tickets, kept for ever: renamed, never archived. Tickets are locked into a batch on the QC and invoice lock screen.
batches.name: Name

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.about: Every change to this project’s records, newest first, as the database wrote it: who, when, from where, the values before and after, and why. Read only.

closing.title: Close the project
closing.about: A closed project changes no more, whoever writes: its assignments are withdrawn and its phones’ unused numbers retired. Nothing in it is deleted. An admin reopens it with a reason.
closing.adminsOnly: Only an admin closes or reopens a project.
closing.nothingOpen: Nothing is still open: every phone is turned in, every ticket QC Approved and locked, nothing waits for a person.
closing.closeAbout: What is still open is said with the close; it doesn’t stop it. Field work for this project that arrives later is held for a person.

qcMark.about: QC is the back office’s own mark: it changes nothing on the record and reruns nothing. Only a QC Approved ticket can be locked as invoiced.

reports.title: Reports
reports.about: What the project moved, in debris totals, never costs. Made each time, like a printout.
reports.emailAbout: To paste into an email, as it stands.
reports.subject: Subject:

exports.title: Exports, photo PDFs and receipts
exports.about: The client package is assembled by hand from these files. Each is made when you ask for it; nothing of it is kept.
exports.photosAbout: Several items a page, each with its details and photographs; or one item a page with its receipt.

layouts.one: One a page, with its receipt

exports.numbersHint: Paste one or more, separated by spaces, commas or lines. Left empty, every one of the days chosen.
exports.receiptsAbout: Paste ticket numbers to get their receipts, or each one’s full record with its photographs and receipt. A number the project doesn’t have is named on the first page.

projects.title: Your projects
projects.about: The projects you are given, read only.
projects.name: Project
